description: A first counted low-demand in-place bilateral takeoff and held landing taught after actual grounded control, conduct and environment checks, without demanding a previous successful flight. Uses one small shallow countermovement with small natural arms and a full reset.

difficultyReview.rule: No source scores are copied from high-output CMJ, squat jump, pogo or forward jump. Null scores are permitted by the existing schema. No athlete skill label or age clearance is inferred.

readiness: Comfortable current bilateral standing and the actual shallow grounded knee/hip lowering, ready-position hold and bilateral rise; actual evidence may come from a prior equivalent or the counted P2 action. Slow held-position control is not recorded as a rapid snap-down pass.

Comfortable unloaded small arm motion at the intended range and understanding of one shallow dip, small upward action, two-foot landing, hold and stop/reset instruction; coach demonstration may supply instruction, not an uncounted athlete jump.

Qualified direct observation, individually fitting protected landing/fall/overhead space, inspected level non-slip impact-appropriate surface, footwear, no cross traffic and current total impact/fatigue budget fit.

No prior successful flight is required. The first actual takeoff and landing are observed within the first listed E1 instructional attempt. Grounded readiness permits instruction only; the athlete may decline, remain grounded or stop without a forced takeoff.

anatomy.laterality: bilateral simultaneous intended takeoff and landing
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes the proposed task, not clinical clearance, injury prevention or a promised performance gain.

whyLayer.whatItIs: One small in-place bilateral jump followed by a held landing and full reset.
whyLayer.whyItWorks: Coaching hypothesis: a protected single action makes first takeoff/landing and response to instruction observable without adding approach speed, distance, rebound or loaded strength changes.
whyLayer.whyItGoesHere: Addresses the explicit first-flight acquisition gap after OR-02 grounded instruction.
whyLayer.programmingGuidance: Place after counted grounded preparation and before fatiguing work, in directly observed individual opportunities with full recovery.
whyLayer.commonMisuse: Demanding prior jumping success, treating a grounded squat pass as a jump pass, forcing height, adding rebounds, or calling planned attempts successful results.

setup: Stationary comfortable bilateral stance with feet approximately hip/jump width, small comfortable knee unlock and arms resting beside the trunk; no approach.
Inspect the actual surface/space and demonstrate the exact action without requiring an extra athlete jump.
Confirm actual grounded-control evidence and stop/reset understanding.
executionSteps: One self-selected shallow continuous countermovement and small natural arm swing, then one small vertical bilateral takeoff. No prescribed jump height, distance quota, overhead arm target, static squat pause, repeated preparatory bounce or maximal effort.

Both feet return to the same personal landing area, with comfortable ankle/knee/hip absorption and organized trunk; stabilize for the declared two-second hold. A recovery step, asymmetry, unintended travel, rebound or loss of control is recorded as a fault rather than credited as a valid stick.
After the hold, stand and settle; full reset and prescribed recovery precede any next listed opportunity. No immediate second takeoff.
coachCues: Land on two feet in your space.
stopSigns: Stop for pain, symptoms, apprehension/withdrawal, restriction, unsafe surface/traffic, lost balance or inability to understand the instruction.

End the affected attempt for repeated prep bounces, unintended travel, asymmetrical takeoff/landing, stiff or uncontrolled landing, extra step, rebound, failed hold or materially changed trunk/knee control.
Do not repeat failed attempts to earn a pass; no extra screening or make-up jump. Select only an independently eligible grounded/slow-position route or defer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: This is a chance to learn a small first jump and balanced finish; you do not need to jump high or prove anything by repeating it.
athleteSupport.painGuidance: Tell the coach and stop the affected action; no forced replacement attempt.

I tried only the listed action.

faultCorrections.beforeTakeoff: If prerequisite or conduct is unsuitable, end the opportunity before flight; explain or use a separately eligible nonflight task later.
faultCorrections.afterFault: Record actual exposure, stop the affected attempt and use remaining time for recovery/instruction; no make-up jump.

coachSupport.groupManagement: One active first-flight athlete per directly observed station; qualified sightlines and waiting-area control must be verified. Do not make the bay count imply simultaneous coaching capacity.
modificationDecisionTree: If grounded-control/conduct/space gates fit, offer first counted flight instruction without claiming prior jump competence.
If only a grounded/slow-position action fits, record that task and zero flight.
If no eligible physical task fits, defer.
